title: African Union Promises to Stop Child Marriage
main_content:
The number of girls married in Africa is expected to double in the next 35 years, experts say.

That means 310 million girls, by 2050 will be married before they reach adulthood, says a United Nations report.

The African Union says it wants to end child marriage in Africa. Delegates at a summit in Zambia are expected to set 18 years old as the lowest legal age for marriage.

Marriage before age 18 is already against the law in most African countries. Yet the UN says that more than 125 million African women and girls alive today were married before their 18th birthday.

Most child marriages involve girls. Some boys ages 17 and younger do get married, but examples are rare.

African Union chairwoman Nkosozana Dlamini Zuma says local culture that undervalues girls and women is to blame. Poverty and lack of education are also responsible, experts say.
